Definition: to inclose; by analogy, to hold back; also to maintain, rule, assemble
BiblicalUsage: To restrain or shut up is the word, and it runs from the plague to the rain to the temple. Aaron stood between the dead and the living and the plague was stayed, Solomon prayed that heaven would be shut up when there was no rain, the king asked who could restrain power enough to build a house for God, and Asa prayed that no man would prevail against the LORD.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the word belongs to God alone in the end, because only He can stay a plague, open the heavens, or hold back the proud. Men try to restrain what they cannot control, and I hold that the prayer of Asa is the right one: let not man prevail against Thee.
